ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the graphs of the functions $y=x$ and $y=ax+4$ intersect at point $A(2, 2)$. What is the solution set of the inequality $x<ax+4$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} By observing the graph of the function, we conclude that when $x<2$,\\
the graph of $y=x$ is entirely below the line $y=ax+4$,\\
$\therefore$ the solution set for the inequality $x<ax+4$ is $\boxed{x<2}$.
